identity.walloon_connection: Born in Frasnes-lez-Buissenal in Hainaut, a Walloon-region locality; the French-language biography identifies the birthplace and places his later life in Braine-l'Alleud.
identity.era_fit: Alive for all of 1936. Belgian Lieutenant-General, former 5th Army Division commander, Chief of the General Staff from 6 January 1917, and commander of Belgian occupation forces in the Rhineland before retirement in 1927.
identity.role_fit: Strong historical commander and security profile for a Walloon Defence Council veteran or strategic commander. He was retired by 1936, so the event should frame him as a senior veteran or council commander rather than an active Belgian staff chief in that year.

The source is a four-person 12 March 1923 group photograph; the exact crop isolates the center figure identified as general Rucquoy by the caption order. No generated detail, retouching, recolour, or identity substitution was applied.
selected_source.uncertainty: The archive title and default page caption foreground Henri Maglinse, while the full caption identifies the center figure as general Rucquoy and the right figure as Defence Minister Albert Devèze. The original negative photographer is not separately named beyond the Agence Rol agency attribution. The public-domain designation and archive identifier are explicit on the Commons Gallica record; retain the attribution above in downstream distributions.
selected_source.face_geometry_note: High-resolution frontal head-and-shoulders view after isolating the center subject: eyes, moustache, ears, cap, collar, upper coat, and both shoulders are clear enough for source review. The larger master preserves the surrounding figures and the original photographic context.
